structured_output.title: One RaceView per sim tick, shared button type CSS, stale docs fixed
structured_output.summary: The game stops rebuilding the RaceView on rendered frames where no sim tick ran (any display above 60 Hz). The view is cached on the Race and cleared after each tick. Duplicated CSS is merged: the button type and transition block shared by .ui-button and .ui-tc, the BEST/NEW BEST tuck-under, and selectors split across two rules. I checked every move against the cascade: specificity is the same and nothing in between sets those properties. The rest is comment, CLAUDE.md and `export`-keyword changes that leave the runtime alone. The sim, the render geometry, the stages and the tests are untouched, so replays, bot laps, scene graphs and stage DOM stay identical.

chosen.why: Real: draw() (game.ts:202) calls raceView(r.world) every animation frame, but the world only changes in tick(); src/driver never touches it. raceView is pure, and its consumers (race-ui.sync, countdownFraming, scene.update, results.update) only read it, with no identity checks. Add `view: RaceView | null` to Race: null in startRace's record and after carViews in tick(), and `const view = (r.view ??= raceView(r.world))` in draw(). Values are identical. Performance item, about +3 lines.

Verified: components.css:122-131 and touch-controls.css:54-63 repeat the button type and transition word for word. Group them as `.ui-button, .ui-tc {…}` right after .ui-button (cursor stays on .ui-button) and delete them from .ui-tc. components.css loads first, nothing else targets the touch buttons, and every later .ui-tc override has equal or higher specificity and comes later, so computed styles are unchanged. Net about −8 lines. The old blocker, #31, has merged.

hud.css:117-125 and :196-200 repeat padding, border-top: 0, border-radius and line-height for BEST and NEW BEST. Use a grouped `.ui-hud-best, .ui-hud-new-best` rule at the .ui-hud-best position and keep the rest in each own rule. Between the old and new positions, only higher-specificity .is-desktop rules match these chips, so computed styles are unchanged. Net about −3 lines. #31 has merged.

Verified split rules. In hud.css, fold :189 (timer isolation) into :31, :192 (best position/z-index) into the single-selector .ui-hud-best rule after C034, and :234 (pos__n display) into :57. In title.css, fold the second .ui-track-card:focus-visible (:127) into :120. Only :124 sits between those two (higher specificity, outline-color only). No equal-specificity rule in between sets these properties, so computed styles are unchanged. Keep the :185-188 comment. Net about −9 lines.

Comment-only, verified stale. components.css:52 names FINISHED (only dead finish-panel.ts uses it; live users are the start title and the results track name). :63 says 'finish stats'. :77 says 'finish card' (live users are the pause card and the countdown roundel). screens.css:1 lists the finish panel. Reword as suggested. For screens.css:1 use 'Pause card, the triple stripe and the full-screen menu ground (results).' No style change.

Comment-only: results.css:1-2 says the navy ground is shared with the start screen, but S6 is dirt in title.css (screens.css:9 already says so). Change it to 'Its navy ground is in screens.css; rows and the roundel use .ui-value type.' Coordinate with C035, which rewrites screens.css:1 once.

Verified by repo-wide grep (src, tests, harness, guardrails): DESKTOP_MIN, DESKTOP_QUERY, outlinePath, SCREEN_CHANGE_MS, KEY_MAP, ACTION_KEY, PAUSE_KEY, PAD_BUTTON, STICK_DEAD_ZONE and stickSteer appear only in their own files. Drop just the `export` keyword. The tsconfig has no declaration emit, so the emitted JS is unchanged. Nothing gates build through these names.

Today is Sunday, so CLAUDE.md may change. Verified: CLAUDE.md:33 says the UI receives view models from src/ui/types.ts, and types.ts:1 says the game loop builds them. In fact game.ts passes the sim's RaceView/CarView to ui.sync (race-ui.ts:44), and race-ui builds HudState itself (race-ui.ts:73, 122). Apply the suggested wording. It keeps the owner's intent (the UI never reads the World) and points the next HUD feature at race-ui. Docs only.

rejected.reason: Real (nine deep imports, countdown.ts:5 included, and props.ts takes three constants the barrel doesn't export). But it re-points import paths across nine files plus the barrel for zero net lines, which is churn under the delete-only rule. It is better done together with a render/UI feature night that touches these imports anyway.

The race-ui line is already fixed (CLAUDE.md:39). What's left rewrites the owner's stated conventions (which folders register content, and the planned cars/features layout). That is the owner's call, not an unattended refactor's.
Same 844×390 literals as C041. Reading the token needs new imports and a constant, so src/ grows a little for a non-performance item, against tonight's delete-only rule.

Real rule violation (raw 844/390 in src/render). But the fix adds a tokens import, an exported constant and imports in three render files: net src/ growth for a non-performance item. Pair it with a render feature night.

The two copies don't share arithmetic: the HUD clamps w/d with 1e-6 and uses the clamped extent in ox/oz, while the card uses `|| 1` only in the scale term and the raw extent in ox/oz. A shared helper needs guard parameters or a wrapper to stay bit-identical, which saves little. track-card.ts is also very likely edited by draft #36 (B11 locked card), and its diff isn't available to check.
Needs an edit to src/ui/stages/start.stage.ts, and screen stages are append-only tonight.

Without C055 (blocked: it needs a stage edit) it would leave the bare 8 in start.stage.ts. A new helper replacing MINIMAP_STRIDE is net about zero lines. Do C025 and C055 together when stages may change.
Adds a helper and an import to src/sim to replace five one-line expressions on hot sim paths. src/ grows for no performance gain, and the risk isn't worth it.
The local helper adds about as many lines as it removes at two call sites. Cosmetic churn.
Types-only alias move: one export plus three imports to delete two local aliases. Net growth for no behaviour or safety gain.
Types-only spelling change with zero net lines. Cosmetic churn.

Grouping would keep computed styles the same, but it moves results-screen stripe rules into screens.css, coupling two stylesheets to save about four lines. Low value. Leave it for a night that works on the stripes anyway.
Moving msToTicks into format.ts needs a new import in countdown.ts: net about zero lines, for two copies of a one-line expression. Low value.
Real (all seven names appear only in their own files), but tonight's eight-item limit is full, and render exports matter less than the UI/input ones in C048. Safe to take next week.
Types-only: adds an interface to deduplicate one inline type used twice. Net about zero lines, cosmetic.
Real but trivial: one `export` keyword on stage-only fixture code that never ships. Tonight's eight-item limit is full. Safe to take next week.

playtest.whatYoullSee: Nothing should look or feel different. Tonight's changes are internal: the game stops rebuilding race data on frames where the simulation didn't step, some duplicated CSS is merged, and some comments and docs are corrected. Buttons, touch controls, the HUD, track cards and every screen should look and animate exactly as yesterday.
howToTest: Race a full lap on the phone: POS, LAP, TIME, BEST and the minimap update as before, and the countdown and GO! clear at the same moment.
Press and release GAS, BRAKE and the steer pads: same font, the same sink when pressed, the same rest fade and wake pop as before.
Set a new best lap: the NEW BEST chip slides down from under BEST, holds and slides back, with the same corners and padding.
Pause and resume a race: the pause card's buttons look and press as before.
On the start screen, tap and focus the track cards: the lift and focus ring look the same.
Finish a race: the results screen shows and fills in as before; RETRY and NEXT RACE work.
On desktop, if handy: arrow keys, Space, Esc and a gamepad still work, and the HUD switches to the desktop layout when the window is large.
